newsitem.title: CHINA: China jails gunrunners to U.S. for up to 14 years.
newsitem.headline: China jails gunrunners to U.S. for up to 14 years.

text.p: A Chinese court on Friday sentenced four people to jail terms of up to 14 years for smuggling 2,000 automatic weapons into the United States, the Xinhua news agency said on Friday.
The guns, the biggest haul of smuggled automatic weapons seized by customs in U.S. history, were part of a deal made by employees of China's biggest munitions merchant, China North Industries Corp.

The Dalian City Intermediate People's Court handed down a 14-year sentence against Qi Feng, former manager of the Duoweidi Science and Technology Co Ltd in Beijing, for illegally exporting the firearms to the United States, Xinhua said.

The court sentenced three others, Lu Yilun, Qin Qixiu and Guo Chengkun, all employees of China North Industries (Norinco) or its subsidiaries, to sentences of three to four years for dereliction of duty, Xinhua said.
U.S. federal agents last May seized the 2,000 AK-47 rifles and 4,000 ammunition magazines, with a street value of $4.0 million, in the biggest haul of smuggled automatic weapons in the United States.
